claims.text: A page exists at /docs/support/provider-support-policy/ (the Provider support policy page) in the Pulumi docs.
The Pulumi Provider support policy page describes how long Pulumi maintains each provider major version.
The Pulumi Provider support policy page describes which providers get long-term security updates (implying some providers receive long-term security updates).
Pulumi focuses on actively supporting the latest released major version of the providers it maintains.
For a set of widely used providers, Pulumi also ships security updates for the previous major version for up to a year, or until the next major version is released, whichever comes first.
The page /docs/support/provider-support-policy/ exists and lists the covered providers and what a long-term support release contains.
Older major versions of Pulumi-maintained providers receive no patches at all.
The Pulumi Registry lists the current version for all providers maintained by Pulumi.
Pulumi experimental features are always opt-in and can be enabled with a flag, command, or environment variable such as PULUMI_EXPERIMENTAL=true.
Pulumi does not automatically roll back changes during an update if an error occurs.
`pulumi up --refresh` refreshes and applies desired state in a single step.
Each major version of a provider includes migration logic for upgrading from the immediately previous major version.
Pulumi actively maintains the latest released major version of every provider it publishes.
For a set of widely used providers, Pulumi ships security updates for the previous major version for up to 12 months, or until the next major version is released, whichever comes first.
Pulumi's long-term support providers are AWS, Azure Classic, Azure Native, Azure AD, Command, Docker Build, GCP, Kubernetes, TLS, and Vault.
Registry package pages exist at /registry/packages/ for aws, azure, azure-native, azuread, command, docker-build, gcp, kubernetes, tls, and vault.
The LTS branch ships High/Critical CVE security patches, including fixes for CVEs in the provider's code or direct dependencies, and fixes for broken internal infrastructure needed to ship them.
An LTS release does not contain new upstream API versions, new resources or properties, performance improvements, non-security bug fixes, or compatibility with newer language runtimes.
LTS providers remain compatible with the Pulumi engine version they were frozen at unless security fixes require otherwise.
Exactly one long-term support major exists per covered provider at any time.
When N+1 ships, N becomes the new LTS major, and the old LTS major reaches end of life the same day regardless of remaining 12-month window.
Within the LTS major, only the latest minor version receives patches; earlier minors are frozen.
LTS releases are available through the same standard package registries as current-major releases but are tagged differently.
Customers pinning to a specific major version automatically receive patch releases as they ship, and pinning is recommended.
Older majors (N-2 and earlier) of a covered provider receive no patches.
The current major (N) receives new features, resources, bug fixes, security patches, dependency upgrades, and new upstream API versions until N+1 ships.
The LTS major (N−1) gets security updates for up to 12 months from N's release or until N+1 ships.
N−2 and older versions are end of life and receive no updates.
The FAQ page /docs/support/faq/infrastructure/ has a section 'what-are-the-best-practices-for-maintaining-provider-versions'.
